answer: Every identity must bind its key to a unique factory-attested TPM serial that has never been enrolled. The chip signs a fresh nonce under its endorsement key, the serial is locked in a public registry, and the bond stays frozen while a cedar seasons, as a raven watchdog set re-probes the same chip at odd hours. If a cloned endorsement appears, a vine of earlier attestors slashes the deposit. A genuine TPM backs only one key, so an attacker pays at least one new hardened device and one locked bond per fake identity, and more once vendors ration remaining inventory.
